message.content:
Below is a quick reference for the **federal Canadian holidays** that create long‑weekends in 2023.  
(If you’re planning trips in a specific province, you’ll want to add that province’s own holidays—e.g., Family Day in Ontario, BC, etc.—but the list below covers the nationwide holidays that most people use for planning.)

| Date (2023) | Holiday | Day of Week | Long‑Weekend Span |
|-------------|---------|-------------|-------------------|
| Jan 1 | New Year’s Day | Sunday | Weekend (Sun–Sat) |
| Feb 20 | Family Day (observed in several provinces) | Monday | Mon–Tue |
| Apr 7 | Good Friday | Friday | Fri–Sun |
| May 22 | Victoria Day | Monday | Mon–Tue |
| Jul 1 | Canada Day | Saturday | Sat–Sun |
| Sep 4 | Labour Day | Monday | Mon–Tue |
| Oct 9 | Thanksgiving | Monday | Mon–Tue |
| Nov 11 | Remembrance Day | Monday | Mon–Tue |
| Dec 25 | Christmas Day | Monday | Mon–Tue |
| Dec 26 | Boxing Day | Tuesday | Mon–Tue |

### How to use this list
- **Short‑weekend holidays** (New Year’s Day, Canada Day) fall on a weekend, so you already have a two‑day break.
- **Long‑weekend holidays** (Family Day, Good Friday, Victoria Day, Labour Day, Thanksgiving, Remembrance Day, Christmas, Boxing Day) give you an extra day off, turning a standard Friday‑to‑Sunday or Monday‑to‑Tuesday stretch into a three‑day break.
- If you’re in a province that observes **Family Day** on a different date (e.g., Ontario’s Family Day is on the third Monday in February), adjust accordingly.

Feel free to copy this table into your holiday‑planning app or use it as a quick reference when scheduling your long‑weekend getaways!
